content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) has established a risk categorization system for foot health in diabetic patients, which determines the frequency of foot examinations based on the level of risk: Category 0: This category represents individuals at very low risk. These patients do not exhibit Loss of Protective Sensation (LOPS) or Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD). They should undergo foot examinations annually. Category 1: This category includes patients at low risk who have either LOPS or PAD. These individuals should have their feet examined every 6 to 12 months. Category 2: Patients in this category are considered at moderate risk. They present with both LOPS and PAD or have foot deformities. Foot examinations are recommended every 3 to 6 months for these individuals. Category 3: This category is for patients at high risk, characterized by a history of foot ulcers or prior amputations. These patients require foot examinations every 1 to 3 months.
